title: Module 2: Application Analysis and Design
description: Planning and design before building: defining stakeholders and roles, inputs/outputs, the data model, client-side vs server-side architecture, UI options, and ServiceNow design recommendations.

questions.prompt: In ServiceNow, user personas defined during design largely map to which platform concept used to apply security?

choices.text: Update Sets
Roles
Client Scripts
Business Rules

questions.explanation: Personas largely equate to roles in ServiceNow, and security is generally applied to applications and their records using roles.

questions.prompt: What is the recommendation regarding the minimum roles an application should define?

choices.text: A single Admin role is sufficient for any application.
At least a User role and an Admin role.
One role per table in the application.
No application-specific roles; reuse the global admin role only.

questions.explanation: It is recommended that every application have at least a User role and an Admin role.

questions.prompt: When planning inputs, what does the "coalesce" consideration address?

choices.text: How frequently the data is received.
What makes a record unique, so duplicate data can be matched and updated rather than re-inserted.
Which role is allowed to submit the input.
The visual layout of the input form.

questions.explanation: Coalesce concerns what makes data unique, which is how the platform decides whether incoming data matches an existing record (to avoid duplicates) versus creating a new one.

questions.prompt: Which input method is suggested for loading data that arrives as a spreadsheet file?

choices.text: A custom Service Portal widget
An Import Set
A Business Rule
A Scheduled Report

questions.explanation: Spreadsheet input is retrieved via an Import Set.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are examples of foundation data that is shared by many different applications? (Choose 3)

choices.text: user
cmdb_ci
task
A custom application-specific table

questions.explanation: user, cmdb_ci, and task are foundation data shared by many applications. Application-specific tables are unique to a given app.

questions.prompt: To represent people in a new application without breaking existing relationships, what approach is recommended?

choices.text: Extend the user table directly so the new app inherits all user fields.
Create a custom table whose name/reference field points to the existing user table, preserving existing many-to-many relationships such as users-groups and users-roles.
Duplicate all user records into a new standalone table.
Store people as comma-separated values in a single string field.

questions.explanation: Rather than extending the user table, build a custom table that references the existing user table, so the established many-to-many relationships (users-groups, users-roles, and so on) remain intact.

questions.prompt: What is the guidance on client-side scripting in a scoped application's architecture?

choices.text: Maximize client-side scripting to reduce server load.
Keep client-side scripting to a minimum (thin client).
Client-side scripting is not allowed in scoped applications.
All logic must run client-side for performance.

questions.explanation: Client-side scripting should be kept thin, with reusable logic placed server-side.

questions.prompt: Which artifact provides a single location for reusable server-side functions, reducing maintenance effort?

choices.text: Client Script
UI Policy
Script Include
Notification

questions.explanation: Script Includes provide a single location for reusable functions, reducing maintenance and time-to-completion.

questions.prompt: When designing the user experience, which of the following are valid ways users might interact with an application? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Standard catalog item or record producer
Workspace
Portal or mobile experience
Update Set

questions.explanation: Interaction options include a standard catalog item, record producer, workspace, portal, and mobile experience. An Update Set is a deployment/configuration-transfer mechanism, not a user interaction method.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are recommended ServiceNow application design practices? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Develop private-scoped applications.
Give every process its own scope.
Track development tasks.
Put all logic in the global scope for easier sharing.

questions.explanation: Recommended practices are to develop private-scoped applications, give every process its own scope, follow delegated development practices, and track development tasks. Defaulting everything to global scope contradicts this guidance.

questions.prompt: An application administrator will need a way to adjust application settings after go-live without code changes. What should the developer do about this?

choices.text: Nothing; settings can always be added instantly at the end of development.
Plan for it during design, for example by including a properties/options module so settings are configurable.
Hard-code all settings and require a new deployment to change them.
Store settings only in client-side scripts.

questions.explanation: Conveniences like a properties module for configurable settings must be planned for during design; they cannot simply be snapped into place at the end of the development cycle.
